description:
PMDA Bug Report: Main library root not scanned after container crash + version upgrade (scan_already_running wedges full scans)
TL;DR

After an unclean container shutdown (host restart on Nov 7), PMDA's startup full-scan resume was skipped as scan_already_running, and the scan engine now treats my main library root as index-only — only the intake root gets scanned. Manual full scans from the WebUI silently find nothing. The legacy folder config (FILES_ROOTS) does not appear to have been migrated to the new v540+ five-folder model.
Environment

    Image: meaning/pmda:latest (log shows v540+ internals; upgraded ~Nov 7, container up 33h since)
    Deployment: Docker on Ubuntu ("gawain"), orchestrated via Cosmos Cloud
    Library: ~100k albums, multi-format (FLAC/AAC), mounted from Synology NAS via NFS at /mnt/nas/data/media → /data/media (RW)
    Datastore: bundled PostgreSQL 17 (/config/postgres-data) + Redis + SQLite (/config/state.db, ~114 MB)
    MusicBrainz: local mirror at http://<ip>:5000 (reachable, working)
    AI provider: Ollama (localhost:11434) — currently refused connection; SCAN_AI_POLICY=local_only

Symptoms

    "Fix this album" fails on individual albums with: "PMDA could not read this folder. Nothing was changed." (e.g. /data/media/music/Phil Woods/The Ultimate Jazz Archive, Set 32_ Swing to Bebop, Modern Jazz (2005) — path exists, 10 FLAC files, perms 1000:65538, rw-rw-r--, dir 777; root can read it inside the container).
    Manual full scan "finds nothing" — no new items ingested from the main library.
    Startup banner: [folders] PMDA now asks for five folders, and this install is missing: /library /intake /organised /quarantine

Key evidence (log lines, timestamps UTC)

Startup (2026-11-07 10:29:xx) — clean config, but wedge in place:

10:29:25 [folders] PMDA now asks for five folders, and this install is missing: /library /intake /organised /quarantine
10:29:27 postgres: database system was not properly shut down; automatic recovery in progress
10:29:32 Config LIBRARY_MODE = files (source: sqlite)
10:29:32 Config FILES_ROOTS = ['/data/media/music', '/data/media/music_incoming'] (source: sqlite)
10:29:33 [watcher] FILES watcher started on 1 root(s): /data/media/music_incoming
10:29:45 [WARN] [startup-resume-sc…] Startup resume skipped for run 374a2db5ca4142e88c66dcbf00b37063 (full): scan_already_running

Automatic changed-only scan (11:31:47) — main library excluded from scan set:

11:31:47 [auto-changed-only…] AUTO scan: starting changed-only scan (pending=52)
11:31:47 [scan:changed_only] effective scan roots: /data/media/music_incoming (from LIBRARY_INTAKE_ROOTS (settings))
11:31:47 [scan:changed_only] Files mode roots reloaded: index_roots=2 scan_roots=1 scan=['/data/media/music_incoming']
11:31:47 [scan:changed_only] FILES mode scan roots: /data/media/music_incoming

→ index_roots=2 vs scan_roots=1: /data/media/music is indexed but never scanned. A full scan over this set can never ingest the main library.
Diagnosis (as I understand it)

    Old container died mid-full-scan (Postgres crash recovery confirms unclean shutdown). The run 374a2db5ca4142e88c66dcbf00b37063 remains flagged as running, so every subsequent full scan is skipped as scan_already_running — including the startup resume that was supposed to recover it.
    The new folder-role model (five folders) seemingly did not migrate my legacy FILES_ROOTS: the intake root got classified as scan root, but the main library root was never classified as /library, leaving it index-only.
    Not a permissions/inotify issue: 524,288 watches available vs. 81,208 dirs; files world-readable; root shell inside the container can list the album folder fine.
    /config bind mount survived the recreation (state.db, settings.db intact and being written).

Questions for the dev

    How do I clear the wedged scan run 374a2db5…? (Is there a safe way — WebUI, DB table, or config flag — or should I just delete the run row in state.db?)
    In the new fold
